messages:
alex_k: quick update — ran a set of nsys + perfetto traces on the kv-heavy generator workload in staging. overheads are larger than our bench runs

mira: how much larger? numbers pls

alex_k: full nsys capture (cuda API + all kernels) raised p99 latency from 120ms -> ~170ms (around +42%) and affected tail throughput. GPU occupancy looked fine but memcpy / kv lookup kernels became dominant in timeline

samuel_r: that matches my earlier microbench concern — full tracing forces sync points and stalls the command stream
jordan_p: do we have per-kernel % time change?
alex_k: yes, quick breakdown from one run: conv/gemm kernels up 5-8% relative, kv_lookup memcpy spikes went from 6% -> 28% of traced time, kernel launch stalls visible. I can paste the perfetto slice view later

mira: ugh. so full traces are too noisy for production. what's the plan for safe profiling?

alex_k: propose layered strategy: 1) lightweight reservoir sampling at 0.5-1% of requests; 2) short capture windows (4s) only on sampled requests; 3) prefer API-only traces (nvtx + counters) not full cuda api unless we hit a regression; 4) automatic rollback if p99 delta >10% during rollout

samuel_r: +1. also add deterministic hashing on request id so sampling is reproducible for a user session (helps debugging)
jordan_p: how do we measure profiler overhead? need a baseline metric we can compute quickly
alex_k: baseline = rolling p99 & GPU warp stalls sampled at 1s resolution. For each canary bucket compare delta before/after enabling sampling. We require: p99 delta < 7% and error rate delta < 0.1% to continue
mira: do we have an estimate of absolute overhead for the lightweight traces?
alex_k: microbench: attaching nvtx + perf counters with nsys sampling mode (no API capture) adds ~1.5-3% p99. Full cuda API capture was the bad actor (~35-45%). So we should default to sampling-mode counters for prod
samuel_r: what about KV cache behavior? earlier you said kv memcpy blew up — is that real or artifact of instrumentation?
alex_k: looks real-ish: sampling shows additional memcpy ops aligned with lookups. Hypothesis: when traced, some async memcpy becomes synchronous because driver forces ordering for accurate timestamps. That amplifies apparent cost. So two benefits of sampling: less driver interference, and lower probe surface area
jordan_p: can we instrument a smaller surface — only mark KV lookup entry/exit with NVTX and collect counters that attribute time without full trace?
alex_k: yes — add TX markers around kv_get and kv_put, emit lightweight stats (hit/miss, bytes) to tracer. No cuda API capture. This gives us enough signal to detect hot keys and unexpected memcpy spikes without huge overhead

ci-bot: deploy-check — canary config updated: sampling=0.75%, window=4s, nvtx-only, rollback_on_p99_delta=10%

mira: rollout plan?
alex_k: rollout: 1% traffic to canary pool for 2h, run comparison job, if metrics ok ramp to 5% for 4h, then 20% for 6h, gate to 100% if stable. At each step auto-monitor p50/p95/p99, error rate, gpu_util, and queue_length. If any trigger fires, immediately disable sampling for that bucket and create a tracing ticket
samuel_r: add a secondary guard: if we see a spike in memcpy kernel time > 2x baseline, immediately stop profiling and capture one short full trace in a quarantined node for offline analysis
jordan_p: agree. we should also limit concurrent profiled requests per GPU to N (e.g., 4) to avoid stress from many sampled requests in same time window
alex_k: implementation notes: feature flag + rollout flag on proxy layer. on request hit: compute sampler(hash(request_id)) -> mark nvtx and emit sample_event to telemetry, then proxy routes to profiled pod with env var SAMPLE_MODE=nvtx. Pod reads env and enables tracer shim. Use reservoir to ensure we don't exceed per-GPU limit
mira: logging/observability? need a short dashboard showing delta and last full-trace anchors so oncall can triage quickly
alex_k: I'll add dashboard: baseline vs sampled p99, sampled rate, profiler-induced errors, avg memcpy kernel time. Also include quick link to perfetto session id if we capture full trace
nata: (typo?)

ops-bot: note — scheduled canary window 2024-12-07T15:00UTC for pool stg-profiles

mira: what's the plan if we hit a regression after rollout to 20%?
alex_k: immediate rollback of profiler flag for affected pool, capture a brief full trace on an isolated node (single trace) for root cause, and open an incident with tagging runtime/perf. Also ship a hotfix to lower sampling to 0.1% until fix

samuel_r: one more ask — add versioned kernel-selection tags to traces (model_version, quantization profile) so we can correlate kernel flips with traces
jordan_p: good call. kernel-selection logs + nvtx markers will help correlate timeline where runtime selected different kernels mid-sequence

alex_k: next steps I will: (a) push canary feature-flag PR with sampler & per-gpu limit (b) add nvtx-only tracer shim and telemetry p99 guards (c) dashboard & runbook updates (d) schedule canary

mira: thanks. please @me on the PR and include a minimal reproducer and perf numbers in the description :thumbsup:

alex_k: will do. leaving raw notes + perfetto link in the ticket once full trace is uploaded.
